gates.evidence: The surface s03 is a subscription paywall page, which is SFW.
The reward is 10 minutes of a premium feature, not cash, ratings, or app installs.
No loss framing is used; it is a standard subscription upsell page.
The offer requires an explicit tap on the 'Play to try' chip before any ad plays.
The offer clearly states 'Play a 15-second game to unlock...'
The user is provided a 'No thanks' button.
The ad appears on the s03 paywall page, not mid-chat.
Eligibility states 'All users, including subscribers' are eligible, which is a negative user experience for someone who already owns the entitlement.

scores.evidence: The offer is placed on the paywall screen (s03) where the user is actively blocked, creating a strong moment of need.
It offers a sample of a paid feature, which fits natively into the UI as a chip.
While time-boxed, the eligibility includes subscribers who already have the feature, which is inefficient and undermines the subscription value.
Cost ($0.0018) is well below the conservative net revenue per view.
Reach is limited to the paywall trigger, which is an occasional occurrence rather than a core daily loop for everyone.
The proposal uses standard SIM-RWD units and existing screens.
Uses app-specific terms like 'Janitor Plus' and '5x context'.
Caps are set to 2/day with a 60-minute cooldown.
Includes a holdout, guardrails, and clear primary KPIs.

requiredChanges: Exclude existing subscribers from eligibility to prevent negative UX and value devaluation.
Correct the eligibility clause to apply only to non-paying users.
Restrict the trigger to the paywall screen (s03) as per the proposal's own trigger description, removing the 'every app open' claim.
parsed.topConcern: The proposal offers an ad to subscribers for a feature they are already paying for, which creates a negative user experience and devalues the Janitor Plus subscription.
